ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The Michaelis equation is expressed in the form $y=\frac{V_\mathrm{max}[S]}{K_\mathrm{m}+[S]}$, where $y$ represents the reaction rate, $V_\mathrm{max}$ represents the maximum reaction rate, $[S]$ represents the substrate concentration, and $K_\mathrm{m}$ represents the Michaelis constant. Simplifying it into the form $y=ax+b$, then $a=\frac{V_\mathrm{max}}{K_\mathrm{m}}$, $b=0$. When a competitive inhibitor is added to the reaction system, the value of $a$ will decrease.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The attached figure shows the reciprocal linearized form of the Michaelis equation, namely 1/V = (K_m/V_max)·(1/[S]) + 1/V_max. The left side of the figure is 1/V, and the right side includes the slope term K_m/V_max multiplied by 1/[S], as well as the intercept term 1/V_max. Then reason: If y = 1/V and x = 1/[S], then this equation can be written as y = ax + b, where a = K_m/V_max and b = 1/V_max. When a competitive inhibitor is added, the V_max of the enzymatic reaction does not change, while the apparent K_m increases. Therefore a = K_m/V_max will increase as K_m increases. So the value of a does not decrease, but increases.

method.method_draft: 先描述图像：图中给出倒数形式的米氏方程 1/V = K_m/V_max · 1/[S] + 1/V_max。令 y=1/V、x=1/[S]，则线性式 y=ax+b 中 a=K_m/V_max，b=1/V_max。再结合竞争性抑制剂的规律：V_max 不变，K_m 表观值增大。因此 a=K_m/V_max 随 K_m 增大而增大，答案为 Increase。
